messages:
olivia: Heads-up: seeing a sharp p99 / latency bump from the Oslo POP starting ~11:05 UTC. p50 flat, p99 +180-320ms across model-serving routes. Not steady — bursts every 30-90s.

samir: noticed this too on the dashboards. traces show kernel selector flipping to the compatibility kernel then back a lot. suspicious.

olivia: exactly. root cause looks correlated with an upstream path change (Equinix -> transit shift). RTT jitter spikes coincide with selector flip.

jin: can you paste a sample selector log and a nettrace?

olivia: sure. here's a condensed snippet from the selector trace during a spike:

```
[11:05:17.132] req=0x7f23 kernel_selector: candidate=fast_attn_v2 estimated_latency=12ms cpu_cost=1.2 -> chosen=compat_gemm reason=latency_estimate_delta(>30%)
[11:05:17.133] req=0x7f23 kvcache: hit=false prefix_len=32 cold=true
[11:05:17.135] net: rtt=42ms jitter=35ms egress_path=equinix-IX -> transit-ABC
[11:05:17.320] req=0x7f23 full_latency=210ms kernel_exec=18ms wait=160ms net_wait=132ms
```

olivia: traceroute around same window shows intermittent timeouts at the transit hop:

```
traceroute to 10.2.3.4 (10.2.3.4), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  0.6 ms  0.5 ms  0.5 ms
 2  equinix-ix.example  1.8 ms  1.6 ms  1.8 ms
 3  transit-abc.example  *  32.4 ms  30.9 ms
 4  onward  34.0 ms  33.8 ms  33.9 ms
```

marco: noisy neighbor on that transit or a route flap maybe. KV cache cold periods + net jitter can push selector past threshold and it picks compatibility kernel which then causes higher memory pathing and queuing.

samir: agree. profiling around the spike shows the continuous-batcher waiting longer for tail requests (batcher wait time jumps). snippet:

```
batcher: window_ms=8 target_batch=8 observed_wait=72ms tail_ratio=0.22
kernel_queue: avg_qlen=6 peak=18
```

jin: two-pronged mitigation idea: 1) temporarily tighten kernel selector sensitivity so it requires a larger delta before switching kernels; 2) raise kvcache warm TTL / prefer cached prefixes for Oslo pop to reduce cold miss pressure.

olivia: +1. also temporarily reduce max batch wait (batcher.window_ms -> 5) for Oslo to avoid long tail waits while the path stabilizes.

ops-bot: deployment request received: change sets planned -> kernel-selector/threshold + batcher/window + kvcache/ttl. Will run canary on 3 hosts in oslo before global.

marco: I'll open a peering ticket with the provider (Equinix + transit-ABC) and attach these traces. tagging net-team.

samir: i pushed a quick patch to lower the selector flip sensitivity (branch: hotfix/oslo-selector). canaries starting now.

jin: reading the post-canary profiler now. early numbers look promising: p99 down ~120ms from peak, kernel flip rate reduced by 84%.

olivia: can you paste before/after sampling?

jin: before:
```
kernel_flip_rate=0.48 flips/min
p99_latency=312ms
kv_miss_rate=0.17
```
after (canary):
```
kernel_flip_rate=0.08 flips/min
p99_latency=190ms
kv_miss_rate=0.14
```

olivia: good improvement. still above normal but moving in right direction.

samir: note — we should not keep the selector loosened forever; that hurts long-term perf for some sequences. this is an incident mitigation.

marco: peering ticket created -> TKT-2026-OSL-PEER. provider acknowledged reroute logs and said they will re-announce stable path. ETA 45m.

ops-bot: canary pass on 3/3 hosts. auto-roll to remaining oslo hosts in 10m if metrics stay green.

olivia: action items:
- samir: follow-up PR to add dynamic region flagging so we can auto-tighten selector only per-pop (ETA: 1 day)
- jin: backfill tests for selector hysteresis (ETA: 2 days)
- marco: monitor peering ticket + share BGP dumps (ETA: ongoing)
- ops: rampback plan if p99 increases > +100ms (runbook step)

samir: starting the region-flagging draft now. i'll include metrics to auto-revert after 30m of stable p99.

marco: provider updated: they completed re-announce, propagation looks okay. traces show no more intermittent timeouts.

jin: rolling out selector change cluster-wide for oslo now. keeping batcher.window_ms reduced until next stabilizing window.

olivia: thanks all. i'll keep this thread updated. we'll do a short postmortem later today to capture the kernel-selector thresholds and a note for net-team to include kvcache pressure signals in BGP ticketing. :memo: :thumbsup:

ops-bot: incident closed -> monitoring for 2h. will re-open if p99 > baseline+100ms.
